title: Nanemoset (Wading River Brook)
summary: Nanemoset is an uncertain brook or creek placename associated with Quaconsit, now Wading River, or nearby fishing tributaries. The name is interpreted as at the fishing-place and is cross-referenced with the related Nemaukak form.
map_geometry_source: approximate Wading River Brook / hamlet marker; Nanemoset location uncertain
history_content: Uncertain brook location, Wading River association, and fish-place interpretation are brought together here. Dated documentary context appear in the Historic Timeline.
translation_content:
Alternate and related forms include Nanemoset, Namoss-es-et, and Nemaukak. The forms are interpreted around the idea of a fish-place or at/about the fishing-place. Earlier placement by De Kay is uncertain when compared with the Brookhaven and Wading River evidence.

Why Place Names Matter

“Exploring the names and stories associated with a place can foster a deep sense of belonging and connection.”

— National Library of New Zealand, Understanding the Context — Place Names and Collective Stories (n.d.), A sense of place section
whereintheworld_content: The point gives a broad orientation near Wading River Brook. The exact Nanemoset Brook location remains uncertain.
